ozet: With the workshop's magic mold, Piko explains list comprehensions: building a list in one line, filtering with if, transforming with if-else, and tiny nameless functions with lambda.

giris.anlatim: Day 13: List comprehensions! In this lesson you'll build lists in a single line, filter them with if, and write tiny functions with lambda.
maddeler: Filter with if, transform with if-else

sahneler.anlatim: Hi, I'm Piko! In the corner of the workshop there's a magic mold: you drop materials in one side, and finished products come out the other. In Python this is called a list comprehension. It squeezes four-line loops into a single line!
The long way to make a new list from a list: an empty list, a loop, and append. The short way is one line! Read it like this: for each n in nums, take n times ten. Both ways give the same result.

ekran.baslik: The long way, the short way
ekran.kod:
nums = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]

tens = []
for n in nums:
    tens.append(n * 10)
print(tens)

print([n * 10 for n in nums])

sahneler.anlatim: Add an if at the end and you keep only the items you want. The mold doesn't let the scores under sixty through.

ekran.kod:
scores = [45, 90, 12, 77, 100, 63]
passed = [s for s in scores if s >= 60]
print("Passed:", passed)

sahneler.anlatim: If you want to pick one of two results for every item, if and else go at the front. To filter, the if goes at the end; to transform, the if-else goes at the front. Keep that in mind!

ekran.kod:
scores = [45, 90, 12, 77]
print(["pass" if s >= 60 else "fail" for s in scores])

sahneler.anlatim: You can write tiny one-line functions with lambda. The left side of the colon is the parameter, and the right side is the result it returns. The same mold idea works for dictionaries too: a dictionary of squares with curly braces!

ekran.kod:
square = lambda x: x * x
add = lambda a, b: a + b
print(square(6))
print(add(2, 3))
print({n: square(n) for n in range(1, 5)})

sahneler.anlatim: Put the else at the end and Python gives a SyntaxError. Remember: if there's only an if, it goes at the end; if the if comes with an else, they go at the front.

ekran.kod:
nums = [1, 2, 3]
print([n for n in nums if n > 1 else 0])

sahneler.anlatim: This mold filters and transforms at the same time. Which list do you think shows up on the screen?

ekran.kod:
words = ["sword", "potion", "ax"]
print([len(w) for w in words if len(w) > 2])

sahneler.anlatim: Five and six! Ax has only two letters, so it got stuck in the filter. The other two words were replaced by their lengths.

ekran.kod:
words = ["sword", "potion", "ax"]
print([len(w) for w in words if len(w) > 2])

sahneler.anlatim: In the tasks you'll make, in a single line, double every number, turn names into capital letters, and keep only the valuable loot. In the challenge you'll write a lambda and build a list of squares.
Today we turned long loops into one-line molds and met tiny nameless functions.

maddeler: Filter: if at the end; transform: if-else at the front
